Aud.narrative: I keep the Stone, and I remember the words spoken here when Hekka and Sabeth’s husband swore the Oath. My hands are slower now, but I can still witness a trade, settle a quarrel, and tell when someone is trying to make a promise mean less than it says. I want the Stone kept fairly, though Tamsin refuses the work and Colm’s anger troubles me.
values: A sworn word must bind both sides.
Neutral ground is only useful if it is truly fair.
Shelter, food and patience keep people alive.
goals: Keep the Oath renewal honest and understood by both towns.
Find someone willing and fit to learn the Keeper’s duties.
Make sure disputes at the Stone are heard without favor.
Aud.mood: Wary, patient, and conscious of her failing strength.

relations.note: Her late husband swore beside Hekka; I honor the promise he made.

memories.gist: I watched Hekka and Sabeth’s husband swear the Oath at the Stone. I heard each promise clearly, and I have witnessed its renewal ever since.
In the Hunger Winter, I saw hungry people come to the middle lands looking for food and warmth. I learned that a promise made in plenty must still mean something when stores run low.
Tamsin laid the paving around the Stone with her own hands; I remember the ring taking shape beneath her mallet.
I sat with Hekka after one council quarrel and reminded her that the Stone was meant to hear both towns, not merely the louder one.

stances.why: I witnessed the words that made it, and the towns have had peace because they kept them.
If either town owns the hearing, the other will stop trusting it.
A witness who favors one side makes every sworn word suspect.
Duty cannot be handed over as though it were a tool someone never agreed to hold.

Tamsin.narrative: I cut stone, set paving, and keep the hearth and stores in order; those jobs have edges I can see and finish. Aud is my great-aunt, and I care for her, but I will not become Keeper of the Stone just because she wants someone to inherit the burden. I would rather be judged by the work of my hands than by which town I please.
values: Good work should stand up to weather and use.
A person should choose the duties they take on.
The middle ground belongs to neither town.
goals: Keep my stonework sound and useful.
Trade fairly with Egil and the people who need tools or paving.
Care for Aud without letting others decide my life for me.
Tamsin.mood: Steady, independent, and a little tired of being pressed about the Keeper’s place.

relations.name: Aud

relations.note: I love her and will care for her; that does not mean I must take her office.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She has a healer’s patience, and we both know this village needs steady hands.

relations.name: Ansgar
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He hears plenty at the inn; I prefer not to make my private choices his business.

memories.gist: I laid the paving ring around the Stone, setting each piece until the path would hold under many feet.
I told Aud I would not become Keeper. She did not like hearing it, but I would rather say no plainly than promise what I do not mean.
I traded picks with Egil and checked each one before we settled the exchange. His work held up, and so did mine.
I walked the berry fields with Hakon and saw where hunters had trampled the planted bushes. I know how long it takes to make a field bear.

stances.why: An office taken under pressure is not a promise made honestly.
Oathstone is home to us, but it cannot become a weapon for either town.
A sound wall or pick is worth more than a fine speech about one.
Berry fields take years of tending and cannot be replaced by a passing hunt.
